item.title: Key meeting to focus on Party building
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Key meeting to focus on Party building Crucial role of CPC's rigorous self-reform highlighted as plenary session set to open One can appreciate the significance of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, which opens in Beijing on Monday, by understanding why Xi Jinping, China's top leader, defined the new journey toward national rejuvenation as a new "Long March" for the Party and the Chinese people. While addressing a gathering marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March on Thursday, Xi, who is also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, framed modern national ambitions through a historical lens, saying that strong Party leadership is vital to the victory on the new journey toward building a modern socialist country in all respects. "We must uphold the Party's overall leadership and the centralized and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee, persistently advance the Party's full and rigorous self-governance ... and ensure that the Party always remains a strong leadership core for the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics," Xi said. The main agenda of the fifth plenum is to study major issues on advancing the Party's full and rigorous self-governance, with the Political Bureau set to report its work to the CPC Central Committee, according to the official announcement. Analysts said the key political meeting, which runs through Thursday, will offer global observers a vital perspective to understand how a century-old political party can maintain its vitality, drive high-quality national development and deliver benefits to the people amid global turbulence. Wang Yiwei, vice-president of Academy of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era at Renmin University of China, said that against a backdrop of global economic slowdown, geopolitical friction and technological competition, many countries are trapped in governance deadlocks. "In this context, China's exploration of the Party's self-governance carries special reference value for other nations seeking stable and sustainable development paths," Wang said. Emphasizing that the self-reform of the Party constitutes the fundamental political guarantee for China's development, he said this demonstrates that ruling parties can sustain long-term governance through self-reform. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, full and rigorous Party self-governance has become a central theme in the Party's efforts to strengthen itself and improve its governing capacity. In December 2012, the central leadership of the CPC introduced the eight-point decision, a set of rules that aim to improve the conduct of the Party, curb official privileges, combat bureaucracy and corruption, and bring the Party closer to the people. The broader anti-corruption campaign and discipline enforcement have been advanced through strengthened oversight, institutional refinement and sustained action to tackle misconduct among Party members and officials. Since 2013, the CPC Central Committee has launched nine rounds of extensive study and education campaigns within the Party in order to guide the entire Party to keep its mission in mind and to always maintain its close bond with the people. In addition, disciplinary inspection — a form of political supervision conducted by higher-level Party organizations over lower-level Party organizations to identify problems, create deterrents, drive reforms and promote development — has played an important role in strengthening the Party. The 20th CPC Central Committee has conducted seven rounds of disciplinary inspections since 2023. The eighth round of disciplinary inspection is about to start, targeting the Party organizations of the Ministry of Education and 31 universities, according to an official announcement on Saturday. With more than 100 million members and over 5 million primary-level organizations, the CPC has resolved the long-standing difficulty of weak grassroots governance through full and rigorous Party self-governance, and has extended Party leadership to every link of national governance. Grassroots Party organizations act as bridges connecting the State and society, ensuring that people's demands are heard and responded to in local governance practices. Despite the significant progress made over the past decade, the Party's full and rigorous self-governance faces new circumstances and challenges amid profound changes in the international and domestic environments and in the evolving situation the Party faces. While addressing the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection in January, Xi emphasized that the fight against corruption is a major struggle that the Party cannot afford to lose, and must never lose. He said the current anti-corruption situation remains grave and complex, and the task of eliminating the soil and conditions that breed corruption remains arduous. It is essential to maintain a firm stance to leave corrupt officials with no place to hide, he added. The fifth plenary session is expected to make new strategic arrangements for long-term and rigorous Party governance, adopt higher standards and take more concrete measures to address the prominent issues facing Party building, experts said. The fifth plenary session is not about "enforcing discipline for the sake of discipline", but is about making the Party itself a more coherent, cleaner and more capable governing instrument, Xia Lu, a research fellow at Renmin University of China's National Academy for Development and Strategy, was quoted by China Global Television Network as saying. Describing the session as "pivotal and bridging", Xia said it is expected to provide a strong political guarantee for high-quality development and the advancement of Chinese modernization. Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, an essential component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is considered to be systematic theoretical guidance for the practice of strengthening the Party. Cheng Meidong, director of Peking University's Institute for Historical Studies of the CPC, said that Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building scientifically addresses the major question of what kind of long-term ruling Marxist party should be built and how to build it, holding practical and long-term significance in guiding the strengthening of both the Party and the nation.

item.title: Europe on high alert after weekend riots
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Europe on high alert after weekend riots Law enforcement agencies across Europe are braced for more trouble after cost-of-living protests turned violent again on the weekend, leading to more than 1,300 arrests in France, mass unrest in Spain, and turmoil in many other countries. The latest protests followed several weeks of disquiet across the continent that led to people taking to the streets in opposition to the fast-rising cost of living, underinvestment in schools, a lack of affordable housing, and, in the case of Spain on the weekend, a threatened state pension system. Some protesters have also cited corruption and their opposition to war as reasons for joining demonstrations. In France, largely peaceful marches ended late on Saturday with confrontations between relatively small groups of protesters and some of the around 70,000 police officers charged with keeping order. Officers fired tear gas and water cannon into the crowds in cities including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, and Bordeaux. France's Minister of the Interior Laurent Nunez told Agence France-Presse the trouble was largely attributable to "several thousand radical activists" who he said had "gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters". Jean-Luc Melenchon, who leads the La France Insoumise left-wing political party and who plans to stand in next year's presidential election, complained that French media has focused on the rioters in a bid to discredit the left, while largely ignoring the grievances of peaceful protesters. He said the riots broke out after the police had created "a setup deliberately designed to provoke chaos". Public officials said the rioting and looting across France on the weekend was on a smaller scale to unrest the country experienced the previous weekend. But despite that, France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry said the latest disorder had caused "hundreds of millions of euros" in damage. France's Interior Ministry estimated that 410,000 people took part in protests across the country on Saturday. Trade unions said the number was more like 800,000. After weeks of such unrest, hundreds of people have already been jailed across the country for acts of vandalism, arson, and looting. At the same time as the rioting in France, more than 120 people were arrested in Barcelona, Spain at a massive student-led protest. And in the Spanish capital Madrid, protesters took to the streets to demand the linkage of state pensions to the rate of inflation and to oppose the possible privatization of state pensions. There were also major demonstrations and riots in Albania's capital Tirana, where police used tear gas to disperse anti-government protesters. And there were clashes in Brussels, Belgium and Lisbon, Portugal, where protesters demanded access to affordable housing. In Milan, Italy hundreds of soldiers helped the police keep order as massive crowds of demonstrators complained about fast-rising fuel prices and the oppressive cost of living. earle@mail.chinadailyuk.com

item.title: Yangling shares farming solutions with the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Yangling shares farming solutions with the world A panel of global experts on Sunday hailed Yangling in Shaanxi province as a hub for innovation in dryland farming and agricultural knowledge-sharing, highlighting how its efforts are critical to strengthening global food security amid mounting climate pressures. They made the remarks at the opening ceremony of the 33rd China Yangling Agricultural Hi-Tech Fair and the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization Agricultural Expo, which have been held jointly for five consecutive years. The events, which run through Thursday, have brought together stakeholders from 51 countries and regions and more than 2,200 exhibitors to promote technology transfer, training and cross-border agricultural partnerships, benefiting farmers in China and Belt and Road partner countries, according to organizers. Dubbed China's "Agricultural Olympics", the events draw senior government officials, diplomats and agricultural specialists from Central Asia, the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. A highlight of the opening ceremony was the release of the 2026 China Arid Area Agricultural Technology Development Report, jointly published by the China Rural Technology Development Center, the authorities of the Yangling Agricultural Hi-tech Industries Demonstration Zone and Northwest Agriculture and Forestry University. The report highlighted Yangling's growing international significance in dryland agriculture. Arid zones account for 41.3 percent of the world's land area and 65 percent of China's cultivated land. Despite water scarcity, these regions contribute substantially to China's grain, meat and dairy supplies. Speakers said Yangling served as a testing ground for agricultural innovation and a repository of knowledge on arid-zone farming. Its advances in molecular breeding, digital field management and water-saving agriculture offer practical, replicable solutions for Shanghai Cooperation Organization member states and other Global South countries facing similar challenges related to water scarcity and agricultural production. Zhai Huqu, former president of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, told attendees that Yangling had evolved from a regional base into an international hub for agricultural exchanges. "Using Yangling as our window, we have shared Chinese crop varieties with grain-producing areas in Kazakhstan, cotton-growing regions in Uzbekistan and orchard zones in Kyrgyzstan," he said. Drawing on agricultural history, Zhai highlighted the benefits of cross-border knowledge-sharing. The introduction of corn, sweet potatoes and potatoes from the Americas centuries ago transformed China's agricultural output and helped support population growth, demonstrating how international agricultural cooperation can deliver far-reaching benefits, he said. T. R. Midhun, deputy secretary-general of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, said the organization's agricultural demonstration base in Yangling had translated exchanges into practical cooperation. Over the past seven years, the base has organized more than 60 international exchange events, provided in-person training for more than 3,000 agricultural practitioners from SCO member states and developing countries, and reached approximately 10,000 additional learners through online courses. "The SCO Agricultural Expo has become a multilateral platform for exchanging agricultural technologies and deepening practical cooperation," said Midhun, adding that the SCO Secretariat would continue to support the Yangling base in expanding cross-border agricultural trade and capacity-building initiatives. Egypt, designated as guest-of-honor for the 2026 event, was represented by Mostafa Ibrahim Elsayad, vice-minister of agriculture and land reclamation. Elsayad warned that climate change, water scarcity and supply chain volatility were placing growing pressure on global food systems. He said international exchanges of agricultural innovations could help countries build resilience. "Egypt believes that international agricultural cooperation is a strategic necessity," he said, highlighting opportunities for cooperation between Egypt and China in smart agriculture, irrigation modernization, agricultural robotics and agricultural processing. Chinese Vice-Minister of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Pan Wenbo described the expo as an important regional public platform for disseminating technologies and facilitating business partnerships. He called on participating countries to strengthen cooperation in food security, agricultural technology, talent development, trade and investment. lilei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xiong'an Vision charts global governance goals
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Xiong'an Vision charts global governance goals Countries endorse plan to strengthen UN, amplify voices of developing world Released on Sunday at the close of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an), a document titled Global Governance: Xiong'an Vision (2026) called for strengthening the United Nations, giving the Global South a greater say in international affairs and translating the principles of China's Global Governance Initiative into collective action. Describing multilateralism as the only viable way to address the global governance deficit, the vision called for safeguarding the UN's central role, improving its effectiveness and enabling Global South countries to participate more fully in international rulemaking, agenda setting and decision-making. It also urged countries to make development a global priority. On artificial intelligence, it called for the UN to serve as a central platform for global governance, with all countries able to participate effectively, share technical expertise and address the technology's risks. The three-day forum in Xiong'an New Area, Hebei province, brought together representatives from 97 countries and international organizations. It established an international advisory committee, released research reports and launched cooperation projects, including the Global South Joint Research Network on Economic and Trade Governance and an International Media Dialogue Mechanism for the Global Governance Initiative. In an interview during the forum, Guy Ryder, the UN under-secretary-general for policy, said the organization needed to adapt as new challenges emerged while remaining faithful to the UN Charter. "The United Nations needs to change as the world changes as well," he said. Ryder cited AI as one issue requiring new approaches. He also said the world was well off track in meeting the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030 and that China's role in advancing global development would be critical. Stanley Kasongo Kakubo, a former Zambian foreign minister, said the GGI's emphasis on fairness and respect for international rules was especially significant for countries in the Global South. He said consistent adherence to agreed rules would give countries greater certainty, helping them build trust and pursue development partnerships. Kakubo also called for a stronger Chinese role in encouraging dialogue and helping resolve conflicts in Africa and other regions. Making tech accessible On AI, Andrea Renda, director of research at the Centre for European Policy Studies, said Chinese open-weight AI models could make the technology more accessible to developing countries because they can be adapted without the cost of building a model from scratch. Access to models alone would not be enough, he said. Developing countries also need industrial capacity to use AI in ways that have created value at home. China's approach to global AI cooperation should help them be "empowered by AI rather than simply being users and consumers" of models developed by others, Renda said. Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of Kazakhstan's China Studies Centre, said the principles of the GGI would ultimately be tested by whether they could be translated into practical mechanisms. She cited the International Organization for Mediation as an example of an approach that seeks to resolve disputes through voluntary agreement rather than determine which side is right or wrong. New mechanisms should earn trust, allow countries of different sizes to participate and produce results that benefit more than just major powers, she said. At a closing news conference on Sunday, Wu Ken, president of the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, said the forum had helped accelerate the translation of the GGI's core principles from consensus into action. According to an incomplete tally cited by Wu, Chinese and foreign participants put forward more than 450 proposals for reforming and improving global governance during the forum. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Desire for better sleep creating opportunities around world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Desire for better sleep creating opportunities around world Market spans mattresses, smart devices made to improve sleeping experiences Chinese sleep technology companies are expanding overseas as consumers worldwide pay greater attention to sleep health, creating opportunities for businesses that combine intelligent manufacturing, artificial intelligence and personalized sleep solutions. The shift is taking the industry beyond traditional bedding, with companies seeking to differentiate themselves through smart products, sleep research and localized services. But turning growing interest in better sleep into sustainable overseas growth will require more than simply exporting products. Chinese brands must also understand local preferences, establish distribution networks and build consumer trust. At the 31st China International Furniture Expo in Shanghai on Sept 8, a smart mattress equipped with a chip attracted attention from visitors to the booth of Chinese sleep technology brand DeRucci. The mattress can automatically adjust to a user's sleeping posture to form a body-fitting curve, while its intelligent system can learn and evolve to provide a more personalized sleep experience. About one-third of visitors to the company's booth were international, according to DeRucci, with many showing interest in the smart mattress and its sleep technology. "Sleep health is a common concern around the world," said David Wu, assistant president of DeRucci and general manager of its overseas markets. However, consumers' sleeping habits and preferences vary with lifestyle, climate and cultural background. Consumers in Western markets tend to prefer softer mattresses with a more enveloping feel, while Asian consumers have traditionally favored firmer support, he said. DeRucci combines its experience in sleep research, intelligent manufacturing and brand development with localized products and services to adapt to different markets. The company began expanding overseas around 2014, with Australia among its first international markets. It now operates in Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Canada, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and other markets. According to the company's 2026 interim report, DeRucci had 53 overseas stores as of June 30. It has developed its international business through a combination of direct retail operations, local partnerships and supply-chain development, rather than applying a single model to all markets. In Southeast Asia, DeRucci acquired Singapore-based home furnishing company MIPL, whose brands include Maxcoil, along with MIPL's production facility on Indonesia's Batam Island. The acquisition in 2023 strengthened the company's manufacturing and supply-chain capabilities in the region. In markets such as Australia, the United States and Canada, it has focused on introducing its sleep products and brand while adapting to local preferences for quality, design and service. Wu said cooperation with established local partners is central to the company's overseas strategy. Local partners bring knowledge of consumer preferences, distribution networks and market conditions, while DeRucci contributes its products, technology and brand capabilities. The company's overseas business revenue reached 260 million yuan ($38.92 million) in 2025, up 67.37 percent year-on-year, according to its 2025 annual report. The company's experience reflects a wider opportunity for Chinese sleep technology businesses as the global market evolves. Hou Wenjie, secretary-general of Shanghai-based research institute Yu Ce Think Tank, said the rise of the sleep economy reflects consumers' growing emphasis on sleep quality as part of health and quality of life. The market spans mattresses, smart devices and other products designed to improve sleep, he said. Chinese companies have advantages in manufacturing, integrated supply chains and the ability to bring innovations into mass production, Hou said. Working with local businesses can also help them adapt to overseas markets and establish distribution networks. Guo Tao, an independent angel investor and an artificial intelligence expert with more than 20 years of experience, said the overseas sleep market is shifting from traditional bedding purchases toward a longer-term sector centered on health and smart technology. Consumers increasingly want more than basic mattress support and are showing interest in features such as automatic adjustment and sleep monitoring, Guo said. The ability of Chinese companies to integrate AI and sensor technologies into consumer products, together with their supply-chain and cost-control capabilities, can help them compete with established bedding manufacturers. Their experience in China's competitive domestic market can also support the development of retail formats centered on product demonstrations and consumer experience, he said. zhengyiran@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Quake-hit county steps up resettlement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after the earthquake. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county. Resettlement and medical care efforts are progressing in an orderly manner in Drachen county of Nagchu city in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, which was hit by a magnitude 7 earthquake on Thursday, as authorities stepped up efforts to provide temporary housing and restore normal life in the affected areas. As of Saturday, major roads in the county remained open to traffic, and power supply to earthquake-affected areas had been fully restored after repairs, reports said. The earthquake affected 13,673 residents of 34 administrative villages in Maru and Gangchen townships, where the average altitude is 4,800 meters. A total of 12,489 people have been relocated, including 7,600 from Maru and 4,889 from Gangchen, accounting for about 91.3 percent of the affected population. By Saturday, all 12,489 people had been accommodated in 1,830 tents at 35 resettlement sites across the county. Given the high altitude and low temperatures, local authorities are setting up prefabricated houses equipped with heating stoves to improve living conditions for affected residents. Relief supplies allocated by central, regional, municipal and county authorities have been delivered to the affected areas, totaling 60,518 items or sets across 20 categories. The supplies include 4,758 tents and 2,000 prefabricated housing units. As of 5 pm on Saturday, the earthquake had left 16 people dead and 76 injured. All the injured had been taken to hospital for medical treatment. Of them, 40 were treated and discharged, while the others remained hospitalized, local officials said. Sonam Kyi, 40, who lived with 11 family members in a village in Maru township, said local government workers had arranged for them to stay in a tent at a resettlement site. "We are living in a tent with 10 beds and two stoves provided by the government, and it's warm inside," Sonam Kyi said. Nangshig Kyab and his family from Gangchen township were also safely relocated to a resettlement site. Nangshig Kyab said numerous cracks had appeared on the walls of his home, making it unsafe to live in, while the yak shelter and courtyard walls had collapsed. Township officials arrived at his village to carry out rescue operations within three hours of the earthquake and promptly evacuated residents, Nangshig Kyab said. By noon on Friday, government-delivered relief supplies had arrived in the village. "We were provided with tents, quilts, bedding, mattresses, heating stoves, instant noodles and other daily necessities, giving us a safe and warm temporary shelter," Nangshig Kyab said. By Sunday, the response had shifted toward resettlement and medical care, with construction of prefabricated houses underway. Tian Lihua, secretary of the Party branch for the Lhasa-Nyingchi area of the fourth branch of China Railway 21st Bureau Group Co, said more materials for prefabricated housing units were expected to arrive in batches on Sunday night and Monday. Once installed, the prefabricated houses provide better protection against wind and cold and offer better insulation than canvas tents, helping residents withstand the harsh conditions of the high-altitude plateau, Tian said. Meanwhile, a magnitude 5.7 aftershock struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 7:25 pm on Sunday, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. BEIJING -- A 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen county of Nagchu city in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region at 7:25 pm Sunday (Beijing Time), according to the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The epicenter was monitored at 32.43 degrees north latitude and 93.99 degrees east longitude. The quake struck at a depth of 10 km. Emergency supplies and temporary housing are reaching residents in Gangchen township, one of the hardest-hit areas following Thursday night's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region. China Railway 21st Bureau Group has delivered warm clothing, instant noodles, bottled water and tents to affected residents. Fourteen prefabricated housing units have arrived, with installation set to begin, while another 20 are expected Sunday night, Tian Lihua, Party branch secretary of the company's Lalin regional division, said. "Once installed, the prefabricated houses will provide better wind protection and insulation than tents, helping residents withstand the high-altitude cold," Tian said. Gangchen Township sits at an elevation of more than 4,600 meters, where nighttime temperatures can drop to minus 6 C. Nang Shigkyab, a local villager, said the family had been evacuated to safety. Relief supplies, including tents, bedding, mattresses and heating stoves, arrived the following day. "We now have safe, warm temporary accommodation. Our lives are stable, and we feel reassured," Nang said. Tashi Samdrub, 37, said a rescue team had provided him with 15 sacks of yak dung fuel free of charge, enough to keep his family's tent warm for about a month. Repair crews from China Mobile Tietong's Xizang branch have restored home broadband and dedicated line services in the county seat of Drachen, as well as a key mobile base station in Maru Township near the epicenter, following the magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday night. The branch dispatched eight emergency vehicles and 17 repair workers to the affected area, which has an average elevation of about 4,800 meters. After 12 hours of work, crews also established a dedicated communication line for the emergency command center, deployed emergency fiber-optic cables and expanded network capacity to support rescue operations. They also installed fiber-optic lines for more than 40 households in temporary housing areas, with efforts shifting toward maintaining stable communications during the recovery. Lhawang Chozang, a China Mobile employee at a service station in Maru Township, said six service stations had been set up across Drachen and Sog counties. "We have restored our network signals, but basic customer services are just as important," he said. The stations provide on-site assistance, free SIM-card replacements for residents who lost their cards in the earthquake, and measures to prevent service suspensions for affected residents and rescue workers, Lhawang said. The company said it would continue network inspections, signal optimization and communications support at temporary settlements during resettlement and post-disaster reconstruction. LHASA -- Rescue and relief efforts continue after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, local authorities said Saturday. The earthquake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday, has left 16 people dead and 76 others injured. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds. As of 11 am Saturday, all 76 injured people were receiving timely medical treatment, with five of the 11 people initially classified as seriously injured having improved to a mild condition, according to the local emergency command headquarters. Meanwhile, relief supplies and rescue personnel continue to arrive in the affected areas. As of 11 am Saturday, 52,450 items or sets of disaster relief supplies had been sent to the quake zone, while more than 2,500 rescue personnel were engaged in relief operations. The supplies include 4,651 tents, 2,000 prefabricated houses, 11,772 folding beds, 5,715 quilts and other cold-weather necessities. A large Wing Loong unmanned aerial vehicle has also arrived at the site. Authorities have established 35 temporary resettlement sites in the disaster zone. More than 1,600 personnel from Drachen county, 347 firefighters from the Nagchu fire and rescue detachment, and 530 police officers from the Nagchu public security bureau have been deployed, alongside vehicles and search-and-rescue dogs. Medical treatment and public health and epidemic prevention efforts are proceeding in an orderly manner, the headquarters said. As of 2 pm Saturday, the headquarters said 949 aftershocks had been recorded in the affected areas, including eight measuring 4.0 to 4.9 in magnitude and 33 measuring 3.0 to 3.9. All temporary speed restrictions on the quake-hit section of the Qinghai-Xizang Railway were lifted on Friday night, according to China Railway Qinghai-Xizang Group Co Ltd. A comprehensive inspection found no abnormalities, and trains resumed normal operations, the company said. Power supply in the quake-hit area was fully restored on Saturday night, according to the State Grid. State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co Ltd urgently dispatched teams to the affected area for emergency power restoration after the quake, the state-owned utility said. More than 300 personnel along with vehicles, power generation facilities and emergency equipment have been deployed as of Saturday to ensure power supply for the on-site command center, provide lighting for resettlement sites and restore damaged power lines. Local authorities said construction on the first batch of prefabricated houses in the quake-affected areas started at around 2 am Saturday. As more units arrive, residents currently staying in tents will gradually move into the better-insulated temporary housing. "We will ensure that affected residents have safe shelter, warm clothing and bedding, hot meals and clean drinking water," said Pan Zhiqing, Party chief of the Nagchu Municipal Emergency Management Bureau. At a hospital in Drachen's neighboring Sog county, many injured residents were sent there for treatment overnight. The hospital has arranged medical treatment and prepared hot meals and daily necessities for patients. Early Friday morning, Norbu Wangchen, a local resident in Sog county, brought more than 100 portions of Tibetan noodles, along with Tibetan tea and tsampa, to the hospital to help those affected by the earthquake. Help also came from the city of Shigatse, some 700 kilometers away from Drachen. Du Guoping, who was preparing to open two new restaurants in Shigatse, postponed the openings after learning of the earthquake and headed to the disaster zone with more than 1,500 kg of dumplings. His team set off at midnight on the night of the earthquake. After a bumpy journey, the team purchased additional supplies, including food containers and bottled water, along the way. After arriving, Du and his staff set up cooking equipment and prepared dumplings for rescue workers and affected residents. They worked during the day, and at night, the six team members squeezed into two vehicles to rest, keeping the heating on to ward off the high-altitude chill. With more than 500 kg of dumplings still remaining, Du said the team planned to stay for at least three days to cook all the food they brought. Watching firefighters, medical personnel and rescue teams race against time at the disaster site left a deep impression on him. "We feel honored to be able to contribute in our own way," he said. Following the magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region, on Oct 22, many temporary housing units have been rushed in from Lhasa, with workers racing to complete their installation. A local Tibetan sweet-tea cafe is serving free hot meals to affected people. Rescue and relief operations continued on Saturday in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, as emergency workers and volunteers rushed to help residents affected by Thursday night's magnitude-7.0 earthquake. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday, has killed 16 people and injured 76 others, with 339 houses reported collapsed, according to a regional government. Authorities said on Friday that three rounds of searches had been completed, with no people reported missing. The regional government upgraded its emergency disaster relief response to Level II, effective Friday, to strengthen rescue operations and assistance to affected residents. In some of the hardest-hit villages in Maru township, rescue teams have been searching damaged buildings, setting up temporary shelters and delivering essential supplies. Volunteers have also joined the relief effort, offering food and other assistance to displaced residents. Sonam Ngodrub, who runs a Tibetan restaurant in Nagchu, traveled to one of the affected villages after the earthquake. "I run a Tibetan restaurant, and there isn't much else I can do apart from helping others," he said. "Every day, I can provide 100 to 150 kilograms of Tibetan noodles free of charge, along with roasted barley flour and sweet tea." Police officers and auxiliary personnel dug through rubble with their bare hands to rescue trapped residents in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday. A 45-member team from the county public security bureau set out at about 11 pm and traveled 85 kilometers, reaching the severely hit villages in Maru township at 12:30 am on Friday. "The only thing on our minds was getting the trapped residents out as quickly as possible," said Tsering Dawa, an officer with the county public security bureau. With temperatures dropping to minus 6 C and aftershocks continuing, 10 officers cleared fallen rocks from roads while the remaining 35 personnel searched for survivors in groups of three. They used drones to assess the damage, coordinated with village officials to check residents' whereabouts, and searched homes one by one. Before heavy machinery arrived, the rescuers used wooden poles to support unstable structures and squeezed through twisted door and window frames to reach trapped residents. They searched more than 200 households and helped transport injured people to hospital. After daybreak, the team directed traffic, transported supplies and set up more than 30 tents to shelter residents. BAQEN, Xizang - Sixteen people have been killed and 76 others are injured following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm on Thursday, local authorities said. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, according to a press conference held on Friday afternoon by the information office of the Nagqu municipal government. Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, urging every effort to minimize casualties. Xi also called for close monitoring of seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters, as well as proper accommodation for affected residents and swift repairs to damaged infrastructure. Premier Li Qiang called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts, while the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM) and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. China has allocated 50 million yuan (about 7.5 million US dollars) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III. More than 5,000 personnel have been deployed to the front lines of the disaster relief operation, working in teams responsible for search and rescue, medical treatment, temporary shelter and the provision of essential supplies. An emergency command headquarters has been established on the front lines to coordinate relief efforts. As of 10 a.m. Friday, 12,489 residents have been evacuated. After three rounds of comprehensive door-to-door checks, no missing persons had been reported as of 6 pm Friday, according to the emergency command headquarters. In a village of Maru Township, one of the hardest-hit areas near the epicenter, Xinhua reporters saw many houses completely collapsed, while others sustained extensive wall damage. Rows of emergency tents were erected in an open, safe area below the village. Half of villager Trinley's house collapsed, burying many of his belongings beneath the rubble. Two white tents were set up in his courtyard. "After the earthquake, our biggest concerns were where to stay and what to eat," Trinley said. "The government provided us with supplies including emergency tents, water and instant noodles," he added. The MEM said that on top of the 5,000 relief items previously allocated by the central government, an additional 5,000 central relief items, including tents, coats and folding beds were allocated. By coordinating efforts with other relief agencies and companies, the ministry said that it has also promptly allocated 43,000 other relief items, including mobile toilets, heating stoves, food and fuel, to ensure that affected people are properly resettled. The Red Cross Society of China has dispatched a working team to the disaster-hit area to guide local relief efforts. It has also allocated 3,800 sets of supplies, including family relief kits, hygiene kits, heaters, tents, jackets, folding beds and quilts. The society has additionally allocated 50 emergency toilet units to support affected residents and coordinated with the Chinese Red Cross Foundation to provide 500 family relief kits, 500 hygiene kits and more than 1,000 cartons of food to the quake-hit area. The China Charity Federation, one of the country's most influential charity organizations, has urgently allocated 3 million yuan to support emergency rescue endeavors. RESCUE CHALLENGES The earthquake zone has an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters. The high-altitude, cold and low-oxygen environment, secondary disaster hazards and aftershock risks pose challenges to the relief efforts, local authorities said at the press conference. Deng Xiaogang, a rescuer with Nagqu's fire and rescue team, said that beyond the low temperatures and low oxygen levels, the biggest challenge was that the epicenter was in a pastoral area, where residents live far apart, making search-and-rescue operations more time-consuming in the initial stages. Some herding sites are up in the mountains, and the terrain is rugged, said Jigme Dorje, deputy head of the Baqen County public security bureau. "At first, machines could not reach these places, so we had to climb up and dig through the rubble with our hands, wearing only gloves," he said. Local authorities said that rescue teams will continue to take precautions to overcome difficulties in relief operations. Nighttime temperatures in the quake zone are low. Earthquake-triggered hazards such as landslides, collapses and falling rocks are currently the main secondary disaster risks. Earthquake monitoring, meteorological and emergency management departments, meanwhile, are coordinating closely to issue timely warnings of aftershocks and adverse weather conditions. Local authorities have launched round-the-clock intensified monitoring of key sites, including mountainsides, reservoirs, power stations, rivers, structurally unsafe buildings and telecommunications base stations. Emergency repairs are also underway, with damaged telecommunications and power facilities gradually being restored. Pan Zhiqing, Party secretary of Nagqu's emergency management bureau, said that in follow-up rescue work, personnel will be assigned to accompany rescue teams to inspect geological hazards along mountains and roads. Dangerous areas will be immediately cordoned off, and people and vehicles will be prohibited from passing. Transportation authorities will monitor road damage in real time, promptly repair and reopen blocked sections, and ensure smooth traffic flow. They will continue to coordinate with meteorological and natural resources departments and issue risk warnings, Pan added. China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom mobilized emergency repair teams, vehicles and equipment overnight, dispatching personnel to the quake-hit areas to restore communications services and inspect network facilities. All telecommunications base stations disrupted by the earthquake in Baqen County had been restored as of 10:30 a.m. Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. The 7.0-magnitude earthquake was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). "An extensional fracture, in simple terms, occurs when the crust is stretched horizontally and, under tension and gravity, faultage slides downward along existing faultage, forming fractures and rupture surfaces," said Han Yanyan, a senior engineer with the earthquake prediction department of the CENC. President Xi Jinping has urged all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, in order to minimize casualties after a magnitude 7 earthquake rocked Drachen county in Nagchu, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, killed 16 people, injured at least 76, and damaged or flattened 339 houses, with search for survivors continuing on Friday. In an instruction issued on Friday morning, Xi noted that the affected county is at a high altitude with low temperatures, emphasizing the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. It is imperative to dispatch emergency rescue supplies, properly accommodate the affected residents, and repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible to safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. In a separate instruction, Premier Li Qiang called for swift assessment of the situation. Given the county's high altitude and the frequent aftershocks, Li urged the Ministry of Emergency Management and the China Earthquake Administration, together with relevant authorities, to strengthen seismic monitoring and forecasting, and step up disaster prevention and response efforts. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently as the temblor struck, with goods falling off shelves and residents rushing outdoors. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas in Drachen, the ground cracked open and sections of a road sank, China Central Television reported. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched 350 personnel and 83 vehicles to support operations in the quake-hit areas. The national earthquake emergency response was upgraded on Friday to Level III — the third highest in China's four-tier system — while a separate Level III national natural disaster relief response was also activated. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corp has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles to aid rescue efforts. The corporation said it is coordinating resources at its disposal to facilitate emergency communication and support imaging of the quake-hit areas. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management have jointly allocated 50 million yuan ($7.5 million) to support rescue and relief operations, while the National Development and Reform Commission has earmarked an additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The Red Cross Society of China has allocated 3,800 units of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves and cotton tents, along with 50 sets of emergency toilets. On the ground, rescue teams have been working relentlessly. In Gangchen township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescuers launched a door-to-door search in the early hours of Friday. In Maru, a resident trapped in a damaged house was rescued around 2:20 am by firefighters who arrived from Drachen. On Friday afternoon, Nagchu Mayor Dondrub said at an on-site news briefing that emergency relief supplies from central and local authorities were being promptly delivered to the affected county. He said that 18 temporary resettlement sites have been set up, providing displaced residents with warm shelter, food, clothing, clean drinking water and medical care. A total of 12,489 people have been relocated, he added. Power supply and communication networks are being restored gradually in the hardest-hit areas. All 628 mobile base stations, which were knocked offline by the earthquake, were restored by 10:30 am on Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. Meng Linghe, Party chief of Drachen, said the quake-hit areas have an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters, which means temperatures plummet after dusk. In addition to the freezing weather, the possibility of secondary disasters, such as landslides, poses grave risks, he said. As scattered snow showers are expected in the coming days, with ice and snow likely to cover high-altitude road sections, Meng urged rescue teams to remain alert and exercise caution when transporting personnel and supplies to the affected areas. Meanwhile, a magnitude 4.5 earthquake hit Zadoi county in neighboring Qinghai province at 10:14 pm on Friday, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km, with its epicenter located around 20 km from the epicenter of the Drachen temblor. Li Hongyang and Liu Boqian contributed to this story. BEIJING -- China has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to aid rescue efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday evening. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) said on Friday that immediately after the disaster, it coordinated and deployed satellite resources to conduct emergency communication support and imaging of the quake-hit area. The CASC said it has activated multiple high-throughput satellite internet emergency service lines for the Ministry of Emergency Management, local emergency management authorities, and major telecom operators. Additional service line terminals are on their way to the quake-hit area. In response to satellite imaging requests for quake relief, the CASC immediately mobilized Gaofen-4 and other satellites to observe the quake-hit area. As of 7 am (Beijing Time) Friday, it had delivered four pre-disaster images and three post-disaster images, providing strong support for rescue and relief operations and disaster assessment. According to the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), a UAV Wing Loong took off from an airport in Xigaze of Xizang autonomous region in the early hours of Friday and flew to the quake-hit area to carry out disaster observation and communication support missions. The AVIC said other Wing Loong teams are ready for deployment. Chinese People's Liberation Army Air Force also sent a UAV around midnight to the quake-hit area for disaster survey. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake struck Baqen county of Nagqu city in Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm Thursday, local authorities said on Friday. BEIJING -- The 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen county of the city of Nagqu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The quake occurred at around 10:33 pm, causing heavy casualties. Focal mechanism solutions show the event was basically consistent with regional tectonic characteristics. The CENC explained that the collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates had caused the uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, crustal shortening and thickening, and widespread plateau deformation. These processes are the main dynamic mechanism controlling tectonic deformation in the western part of the Chinese mainland. The interior of the plateau is subjected to both north-south compression and east-west extension, and two typical fault systems, trending roughly north-south and east-west, have developed there. "The epicenter is located within the Changtang block of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, about 2 km from the nearest fault, the Baqen-Riwoqe fault," Han said. Under such intense crustal deformation, the Changtang block and its surrounding fault zones are particularly active. Since 1900, the block has experienced six earthquakes of magnitude 7 or above, including this one. The largest was a 7.5-magnitude earthquake in Shuanghu on Nov 8, 1997. "Therefore, this earthquake was an energy release of the Changtang block," Han said. Authorities in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, warned at a Friday news conference that aftershocks and secondary disasters remain major risks following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county on Thursday night. The quake had killed 16 people and injured 76, said Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu. The affected area averages nearly 4,800 meters in elevation, according to Meng Linghe, Drachen's Party secretary. Landslides, slope collapses, and falling rocks are the main secondary geological hazards. Low nighttime temperatures, scattered snow showers, and black ice on shaded high-altitude roads pose risks to rescue vehicles. Dondrub said inspections have covered 12 roads spanning more than 1,700 kilometers, 201 bridges, and 324 culverts. Officials identified 11 hazards and cleared rockfalls at seven road locations. Earthquake, meteorological, and emergency management departments are consulting and issuing aftershock and weather warnings, while police and transport authorities keep emergency routes open. Round-the-clock monitoring and emergency repairs cover mountain slopes, reservoirs, power stations, river channels, unsafe buildings, and telecommunications base stations. Authorities are inspecting mountain slopes and roads alongside rescue teams, Meng said. Dangerous areas will be cordoned off, and search operations will be kept away from steep slopes. Authorities will inspect geological hazard sites and vulnerable infrastructure hourly and continue issuing updated risk alerts, Dondrub said. China's transport authorities have stepped up road inspections and emergency support to ensure rescue vehicles can reach areas affected by a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. Roads in the quake-hit area are under traffic controls, with access maintained for rescue vehicles while other vehicles are temporarily barred, according to the Ministry of Transport. The earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday. By 10 am Friday, 16 people had been killed and 76 injured, according to local authorities. The ministry activated a Level III emergency response for road transport at 9 am Friday and dispatched a team to coordinate rescue support and efforts to keep roads open. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Finance to arrange emergency funding for road clearance and repairs. Level III is the second-lowest level in the ministry's four-tier response system, with Level I being the highest. Xizang's transport department activated its own Level II response after the earthquake. Local highway authorities deployed 178 personnel and 39 pieces of machinery to inspect affected sections of five national highways and seven provincial roads. They have checked 2,377 kilometers of roads, 295 bridges and 635 culverts. The inspections found varying degrees of damage along sections of national highway G345 and provincial highway S301. More detailed inspections of roads, bridges and other transport infrastructure are continuing. Emergency equipment is being sent to the disaster-hit area from reserve centers in Lhasa and Qamdo to help crews clear debris and repair roads. Crews from nearby construction projects run by centrally administered State-owned enterprises, along with other road maintenance teams, are on standby to provide additional support. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. State Grid Xizang Electric Power activated its emergency response and dispatched teams overnight to Gangche and Maru townships to inspect and secure power facilities. Electricity has been restored across the area surrounding the Maru township government offices. Phone and internet services have also returned to normal in two villages in the township. Being close to the earthquake's epicenter, they were among the most affected areas. According to the administration, the earthquake knocked 628 mobile base stations offline, accounting for 8.5 percent of the city's total. These stations have been restored as of 10:30 am Friday, bringing communications in the affected area back to pre-earthquake levels within 12 hours. The administration said 131 emergency repair personnel and 50 vehicles had been deployed to restore communications, along with 38 generators and other emergency equipment. Telecommunications networks in the disaster area are now operating normally, supporting the coordination of rescue operations. Earthquake authorities in Yunnan and Sichuan provinces have sent a dozen personnel to the affected area to assess the quake's intensity, verify damage, and conduct other emergency field operations. Sixteen people have been killed and 76 injured as of 1 pm Friday following Thursday's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, officials said at a news conference Friday. Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu city, which administers the county, said rescuers had completed three rounds of searches, checking key areas and visiting residents in remote, scattered settlements. Authorities have set up 18 temporary shelters and relocated 12,489 people, he said. Due to the quake, 339 households have collapsed or been damaged, along with 20 livestock sheds. The immediate priorities are treating the injured and ensuring displaced residents have access to basic necessities, he said. Authorities will provide insulated tents and hot meals, with particular attention to older people, children, pregnant women, new mothers, and people with disabilities. Rescuers went door to door in villages near the epicenter of a magnitude-7.0 earthquake that struck Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, looking for anyone in need of help. In Gangche township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescue workers began searching for people trapped in their homes in the early hours of Friday morning. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently, with goods tumbling from shelves as residents rushed outside to escape the quake on Thursday night. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas, the earthquake cracked the ground and caused sections of road to sink, China Central Television reported. "Suddenly, there was a tremendous rumbling. For a moment, it felt as if hundreds of yaks were running at once," said Dzondru Tseltrim, a resident of Garuthang village in the county. His family had already gone to bed when the shaking began. Woken by the tremors, he heard cabinets and wooden pillars creaking inside the house. He rushed to wake his father, in his 80s, and helped him outside. Other family members soon followed. Fearing aftershocks, the family decided not to sleep indoors that night. They arranged for his father to rest in a car while the others prepared to spend the night in the courtyard. BEIJING -- China has allocated 50 million yuan (about $7.5 million) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The earthquake struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday, leaving 16 people dead and 65 injured. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 am on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 am on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials. The number of people injured in the 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Drachen county in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, has risen to 65, including 11 seriously injured and 54 with minor injuries, according to the city's earthquake relief headquarters. As of 10 am Friday, rescue teams had safely evacuated 12,489 residents from affected areas. Search and rescue operations, damage assessments, and efforts to provide temporary shelter for displaced residents are ongoing. By early Friday, rescue teams and relief supplies reached earthquake-hit Drachen county in Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region, as authorities upgraded the national earthquake emergency response to Level III, the third highest of the four-tier system, the Ministry of Emergency Management said on Friday. A 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck the county at 10:33 pm on Thursday, killing 16 people and injuring 54. A working team from the central government has been dispatched to the disaster area to guide and assist relief efforts. The ministry has guided the Xizang autonomous region's emergency management department to send Wing Loong drones to the disaster area to assess the damage. By 4:30 am on Friday, relief supplies allocated by authorities at the central, autonomous region, city, and county levels had arrived in the disaster area. The relief supplies comprised of 1,000 prefabricated housing units, about 3,200 tents, about 2,800 folding beds, and 100 mattresses, along with quilts, stoves, cotton clothing, overcoats, and Tibetan robes. Also included were four generators, 1,000 hand-crank solar flashlights, and 1,000 head-mounted outdoor lights. By 6:30 am on Friday, 120 personnel and 27 vehicles had arrived in the disaster area. Another 230 personnel and 56 vehicles from the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps were en route, having reached Nagchu. The Red Cross Society of China has activated an emergency response on Friday, allocating 3,800 sets of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves, cotton tents, windproof jackets, folding beds, and cotton quilts. It has also dispatched a working group to the disaster zones to guide local efforts in relocating affected residents.

item.title: Chinese opera hits big in small theaters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Tradition turns intimate as audiences get a close-up look at how various styles are created, performed, and expressed, Chen Nan reports. Li Chanchan and Fan Yuyan, two young students from the National Academy of Chinese Theatre Arts in Beijing, drew a crowd in a courtyard as they demonstrated a traditional jaw-dropping feat before one unleashed a burst of fire. The flames flared and vanished in an instant, prompting gasps and applause from spectators gathered among the courtyard's gray bricks and tiled roofs. The demonstration is a signature Qinqiang Opera stage skill: fire-breathing, known for its dramatic visual impact. Other performers demonstrated the sweeping spear movements of Peking Opera, offering a glimpse of the physical precision and theatrical spectacle that has sustained traditional Chinese opera for generations. At the 13th Xiqu Opera Black Box Festival, which opened at Star Theaters in Beijing on Oct 14, tradition is also being explored through more intimate, unexpected storytelling forms. The festival runs through Nov 22 and brings together 16 productions tailored for smaller theaters spanning 11 traditional Chinese opera genres, including Peking Opera, Kunqu Opera, Yuju Opera, Pingju Opera, and Cantonese Opera. The opening performance, The Face in the Mirror, a Huaiju Opera production, takes audiences into a world of illusion and psychological unease, asking what happens when people finally obtain what they desire.

item.title: Promoters bear fruit for farm labor
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Promoters bear fruit for farm labor Agri-produce brokers develop versatile role as livestreamers, market connectors In a sunlit orchard in Xi'an, Shaanxi province, Li Qian peeled a kiwifruit, took a bite and let the juice run down his hand. "Our kiwifruit is 90 percent sweet and 10 percent sour, with thin skin and thick flesh," he said to online viewers. "Every one is as good as the one in my hand. If you like kiwifruit shipped directly from the place of origin, place an order and try it!" More than 300,000 orders, with over 10,000 repeat buyers, were placed on the platform he posted the video on. "People like watching me eat," Li said with a laugh. "Many had no need to buy kiwifruit but after watching the video, they placed an order. You could say I created consumer demand." Li represents a new generation of agricultural product brokers, whom the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs calls "an important link connecting small farmers with the big market". Beyond simply promoting goods, many brokers are involved in ensuring product quality, making connections between growers and markets, and improving farm incomes. Four years ago, a glut of unsold kiwifruit in Li's hometown Zhouzhi, Xi'an, lured the international trade graduate into the field. Now, he is one of the leading product brokers. And as China is advancing all-around rural vitalization, their role is becoming more formalized. A State Council plan for accelerating agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period proposes training 30,000 prominent agricultural product brokers.

ZXMOTO motorcycle founder sets Guinness record for longest ride on open water Share - WeChat
Zhang Xue, the founder of Chinese motorcycle manufacturer ZXMOTO, set a new Guinness World Record on Sunday in his hometown of Mayang Miao autonomous county, Huaihua, Central China's Hunan province. Riding a modified MX450 across open water for 40.74 kilometers, Zhang set a new record for the greatest distance traveled over open water by a modified motorcycle, surpassing the previous record of 31.8 km.
